title: What is cohesion, why is HIGH cohesion a design goal (SRP: each class does one thing), and what does LOW cohesion look like (God class doing unrelated tasks)?
shortTitle: What is cohesion and why is high cohesion a design goal?
keyPoints: Cohesion measures how closely related the responsibilities within a single class are
High cohesion: all methods and fields serve one clear purpose (SRP: Single Responsibility Principle)
Low cohesion: God class doing many unrelated things (accounts, trades, notifications, reports in one class)
High cohesion enables: understandability (one purpose), testability (test one thing), changeability (modify without breaking others)
The AND test: describe the class in one sentence; if you use AND, the class has too many responsibilities
The ideal design is high cohesion (focused classes) plus loose coupling (interfaces and dependency injection)

s1_definition.oneliner: High cohesion means one class, one purpose, all methods related (SRP). Low cohesion means a God class doing many unrelated things. The goal: high cohesion plus loose coupling equals clean design.
s1_definition.profdef:
Cohesion measures how closely related the responsibilities within a single class are.

- **High cohesion**: all methods and fields serve one clear purpose. `FeeCalculator` only calculates fees (Single Responsibility Principle).
- **Low cohesion**: the class does many unrelated things. A God class `BankingManager` handles accounts, trades, notifications, reports, and compliance in one 3000-line class.
- **Benefits of high cohesion**: understandability (one purpose = easy to read), testability (test one thing in isolation), changeability (modify fees without touching notifications), reusability (use FeeCalculator anywhere without dragging unrelated code).
- **The AND test**: describe the class in one sentence. If you use AND, the class has too many responsibilities.
- **Ideal design**: high cohesion (focused classes) + loose coupling (interfaces + DI) = clean, maintainable, testable code.
s1_definition.analogy: High cohesion: National Bank of India has separate counters: one for deposits, one for loans, one for forex. Each counter does one thing well. Need to change loan processing? Only the loan counter changes. Low cohesion: one clerk handles deposits, loans, forex, complaints, and makes coffee. Overwhelmed, error-prone, and if the clerk is sick, everything stops. That clerk is a God class.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Cohesion measures how closely related the responsibilities within a single class are. High cohesion means all methods and fields serve one clear purpose. FeeCalculator only calculates fees. AccountService only manages accounts. Low cohesion means the God class anti-pattern with 3000 lines handling accounts, trades, fees, notifications, and compliance. High cohesion is a design goal because it enables understandability (one purpose = easy to read), testability (test one thing in isolation), changeability (modify fees without touching notifications), and reusability (use FeeCalculator anywhere without dragging unrelated code).

The AND test: describe the class in one sentence. If you use AND, the class has too many responsibilities. BankingManager manages accounts AND executes trades AND calculates fees AND sends notifications: four ANDs = four classes needed. FeeCalculator calculates trading fees: no AND = high cohesion.

Remember one sentence: high cohesion means one class, one purpose, all methods related, and the AND test catches God classes that need to be split.
